# requireGridRangeContainedIn

<link-summary>Returns the range once it is known to lie within another, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireGridRangeContainedIn() — Returns the range once it is known to lie within another, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireGridRangeContainedIn(
  gridRange: GridRange,
  containerGridRange: GridRange,
  message?: string
): GridRange;
```

The assertion form of `isGridRangeContainedIn`. The default message names both ranges in A1 notation, which is what makes the failure readable in an execution log.

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type        | Description                                                                      |
| :--------------------- | :---------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `gridRange`            | `GridRange` | The grid range that must be contained.                                           |
| `containerGridRange`   | `GridRange` | The grid range expected to contain it.                                           |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`    | The message of the exception. A default naming both ranges is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`GridRange` — the first range, unchanged.

## Throws

| Exception                   | Condition                                       |
| :-------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------- |
| `InvalidGridRangeException` | the first range is not contained in the second. |

## Examples

### Guarding a write

```javascript
const inner = { startRowIndex: 1, endRowIndex: 2, startColumnIndex: 1, endColumnIndex: 2 };
const outer = { startRowIndex: 0, endRowIndex: 5, startColumnIndex: 0, endColumnIndex: 5 };

requireGridRangeContainedIn(inner, outer); // => the inner range
```
